newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: OLYMPICS-S.AFRICAN POLICE GIVE GAMES PAY WARNING.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-S.AFRICAN POLICE GIVE GAMES PAY WARNING.

text.p: A South African police union said on Monday the government will have to spend more money on the force if the Olympic Games are to be held in Cape Town in 2004.
An evaluation report on the 11 cities bidding for the Games released last week noted that it would be a challenge for South Africa to address the concerns over crime in Cape Town.
But the South African government, committed to reducing its budget deficit, has placed a moratorium on recruiting new police officers and has cut police spending to the bone.

"If they want the Olympics in the Western Cape, and crime is a problem, then they must put their money where their mouth is and get more cops on the beat," said Andy Miller, provincial secretary of the South African Police Union for Western Cape province, which includes Cape Town.
He said police needed more and better equipment as well as pay increases to improve their morale.

"They're going to be wanting the poor cops to work 16 hours around the clock (if Cape Town hosts the Olympics) and obviously they're not going to do it unless they get paid for it," Miller said, adding that police overtime had not been budgeted for in drafting the city's Olympic bid.
The head of Cape Town's Olympic bid campaign, Chris Ball, said last week he was confident the city would be on the shortlist of five contenders to be announced next month.
